name: CALM (Co-evolution of Algorithms and Language Model)
org: City University of Hong Kong, Southeast University, University of Victoria, Hon Hai Research Institute
one_liner: Heuristic evolution where the LLM itself is also fine-tuned with reinforcement learning on how good its heuristics are.

loop.proposes: Heuristic code from a small LLM inside an evolutionary search
loop.judged_by: Running the heuristic on problem instances to get a quality score that becomes the RL reward
loop.steers: Verbal guidance through prompts plus numerical guidance through GRPO fine-tuning of the LLM weights

headline_result: A Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model (INT4, on a single 24GB GPU) with GRPO fine-tuning reached an average 0.71% gap on online bin packing, against 0.89% for MCTS-AHD and 2.40% for Best Fit, and beat the best listed competitor on CVRP (3.95% vs 4.70%) and OP (12.58% vs 16.34%) at N=200 in the paper's tables.
caveat: The advantage is not uniform: on TSP at N=50 MCTS-AHD (9.69%) beats CALM (10.04%). Numbers come from the paper's own tables and baselines, which mostly ran on GPT-4o-mini.
beyond_harness_note: Beyond a harness, the feedback also updates the generator's weights by RL while an evolutionary search runs, and the result is a heuristic that works without the model.
generative_model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, INT4, fine-tuned with GRPO (about 1.15% of weights)

sources.title: CALM: Co-evolution of Algorithms and Language Model for Automatic Heuristic Design

verification.notes: Resolved arXiv:2505.12285 (Huang, Wu, Wu, Wang, Lee, et al.; v1 18 May 2025). From the HTML tables: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct INT4, GRPO (not PPO), 24GB GPU, tasks OBP/TSP/CVRP/OP. Draft claim '7B INT4 on 24GB' confirmed; added that the RL method is GRPO and that CALM does not win every setting. Org confirmed from the arXiv HTML (review 2026-11-03).
